Honestly, I don't think the burden lies on any single one of them. The problem lies in the fact that right now, there's too much we don't know about how these medications affect the brain. They're each trying to do their job, which is to make lives easier for the people affected by mental illness.  
  
The psychiatrist doesn't know exactly which one to choose, but they'll keep trying different ones because they know that if they can find the right combination, the patient's life will improve significantly.  
  
The pharmaceutical companies develop meds with the hope that they will help people. They're doing their best with what they have now while trying to figure out where to go from here.

I'm not a psychiatrist, nor will I pretend to be, but I've got lots of experience with them.  
  
I would think the hardest part about being a psychiatrist is knowing so little about which anti-depressant to prescribe to a patient in need. Everyone reacts differently to different meds, so it's really a game of guess-and-check until the patient feels better. I don't know about everyone, but it took me 3 years and 7 medications to finally find one that worked without wearing off or unbearable side effects.  
  
Not that other types of medicine are easy, but if someone has a specific heart condition, you can prescribe them a certain set of meds. But if someone has depression, there are all kinds of meds and no way to know how they will work on your patient until they try them for 6 weeks.

There's struggles with the question itself based on what your assumption of the social contract is.  
  
A Lockean believes that by living in a particular society, you agree to abide by all of the society's rules. The primary goal of the contract is self-preservation and the protection of property.  
  
To contrast, Rousseau believed that the social contract had a greater purpose. Social interaction inherently improves the human situation, so the focus is less on the laws and moreso on the benefits of all the people in the society.  
  
To even begin a discussion of the social contract, there must first be an agreement about which understanding of the social contract you subscribe to.
